name: RaDA: Retrieval-augmented Web Agent Planning with LLMs
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024 (ACL Findings 2024), Bangkok, Thailand, pages 13511-13525. ACL Anthology ID 2024.findings-acl.802; DOI 10.18653/v1/2024.findings-acl.802; DBLP conf/acl/KimBKGH24.

code_url: https://github.com/ldilab/RaDA (official repo; the paper footnote states 'Code is available at: https://github.com/ldilab/RaDA', and the repo is titled '[ACL 2024-findings] RaDA: Retrieval-augmented Web Agent Planning with LLMs' linking to the ACL Anthology page. Note: as of retrieval the public repo contains only a README placeholder -- 1 commit, no released code files).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no continuously-updated leaderboard or paper-list maintained by the authors; the work is a single research repo).
task_domain: web (LLM-based Web/computer-control agents performing task automation via planning and grounded action generation on web environments).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, exemplar-free (no human-engineered few-shot prompts) Web-agent planning with a frozen LLM backbone (GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 and GPT-4-0613 via the OpenAI API). Given a natural-language task instruction, the agent must produce a sequence of grounded actions (e.g., click/type/select over HTML elements) executed in a web environment. Supervision comes only from a retrieval corpus of previously collected successful trajectories (48 base MiniWoB tasks for CompWoB; the Mind2Web training-set trajectories for Mind2Web) -- no gradient training of the LLM or the retriever, and no manually authored task-specific exemplars. The setting explicitly targets unseen and compositional (complex) tasks and the compositional-generalization failure of LLM agents. RaDA disentangles planning into Retrieval-augmented Task Decomposition (RaD) and Retrieval-augmented Action Generation (RaA), with a subtask-completion verifier closing the loop step by step.
what_is_retrieved: demos / trajectories: dynamically retrieved exemplars, i.e., (partial) trajectory demonstrations of similar previously-seen tasks/subtasks (each exemplar is a task/subtask description plus its demonstrated action trajectory). These exemplars are retrieved both for task decomposition (queried by the overall task T) and for per-subtask action generation (queried by a subtask-compositional query).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: retrieval targets a fixed, pre-collected corpus of successful trajectories (48 MiniWoB base-task trajectories for CompWoB; Mind2Web training-set trajectories for Mind2Web). The corpus is constructed offline and is NOT grown/written by the agent at test time. The paper lists collecting new exemplars during deployment as future work, confirming the store is static/frozen.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: the dense retriever outputs the top-k exemplars with k set to 3 (a fixed hyperparameter). There is no completeness/minimal-set recovery objective or precision-driven variable-size recommendation for the retriever; RaDA's contribution is reformulating the QUERY (subtask-compositional) and the granularity of retrieval rather than the ranking objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Partial: Retrieve (yes -- dense retrieval of exemplars), Reuse (yes -- retrieved exemplars are reused as in-context demonstrations to ground decomposition and action generation), Revise (partial -- a subtask-completion verifier re-formulates the query and tracks plan state, but retrieved cases are not explicitly edited/repaired into new solutions), Retain (no -- nothing is written back to the corpus). Flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial, Retain: no].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as retrieval-augmented planning / in-context learning with exemplar retrieval, inspired by human cognitive abstraction and memory reuse (Lachmy et al. 2022; Zhao et al. 2022; Sumers et al. 2023).
retrieval_unit: single demo / (sub-)trajectory: a retrieved exemplar is a task- or subtask-level trajectory demonstration (task/subtask description plus its action sequence in the web environment). RaDA's key distinction from Synapse is that it can retrieve PARTIAL (subtask-level) trajectories rather than whole-task trajectories, enabling the use of partial/sub-trajectory exemplars per subtask.
index_source: Static, offline-induced corpus: the retrievable store is built from successful trajectories collected offline (48 MiniWoB base tasks for CompWoB; Mind2Web training-set trajectories for Mind2Web). It is not test-time-induced and does not grow during deployment.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: a dense embedding index over exemplar task/subtask descriptions (and additional state/task metadata) encoded with pre-trained sentence embeddings (text-embedding-ada-002), ranked by cosine similarity. No graph, hierarchical, or cluster topology is imposed on the index itself (though planning over subtasks is hierarchical, the retrieval index is a flat embedding store).
retriever_type: Dense retriever: dense passage-retrieval-style retrieval using pre-trained sentence embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002), with cosine similarity, following the Synapse (Zheng et al., 2024b) retriever setup. Off-the-shelf, not BM25 / not generative / not LLM-as-retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): the retriever uses frozen pre-trained embeddings (text-embedding-ada-002) with cosine similarity; it is NOT trained with contrastive similarity labels, LM-feedback, downstream-task effectiveness, or RL. The paper's Limitations explicitly note that retriever finetuning was not considered and is left to future work. RaDA's novelty is in query construction/granularity, not retriever learning.
query_construction: Two distinct query formulations: (1) for RaD (decomposition) the query is the raw overall task instruction T; (2) for RaA (action generation) the query is a 'subtask-compositional query' Q_T formed by concatenating the currently relevant/remaining subtasks (Q_T = gamma_1 (+) gamma_2 (+) ... (+) gamma_m), where subtasks are produced by the decompositional planner and updated by the verifier. This composed query can range from a single focused subtask to all remaining subtasks. So the query is decomposition-derived and dynamically reformulated, not just the raw input.
query_granularity: Both task-level and subtask/step-level (two-level retrieval): retrieval is done once at the task level with T for decomposition (RaD), and then repeatedly at the subtask level with the subtask-compositional query Q_T during iterative action generation (RaA). The subtask-level query is reformulated each iteration via the verifier.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative: one task-level retrieval at decomposition time (RaD), then iterative subtask-level retrieval during the RaA action-generation loop (a new retrieval per reformulated subtask-compositional query until all subtasks are completed). A 'decomposition trigger' gates whether decomposition is invoked (always on for CompWoB; on Mind2Web triggered when task length exceeds the minimum-length exemplar by 50%).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule plus a length-based decomposition trigger: retrieval is invoked on a deterministic schedule (at decomposition, then once per remaining-subtask iteration). The decision to DECOMPOSE (and thus enter the subtask-retrieval loop) uses a simple rule/trigger: always triggered on CompWoB; on Mind2Web triggered if the task length exceeds the minimum-length exemplar by 50% (an oracle decomposition trigger is also used in some reported full-set runs). There is no token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, learned-complexity-classifier, or reflection-token trigger.
reranking: None: the dense retriever produces a cosine-similarity ranking and the top-k (k=3) exemplars are taken directly; no cross-encoder, hierarchy-aware, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranking stage is applied.
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose plus light deduplication: rather than refining the retrieved text itself, RaDA refines WHAT is retrieved by decomposing the task and issuing subtask-scoped (compositional) queries, so each LLM call sees only the relevant subtask exemplars (reducing context). For the RaA ablation baseline, redundant exemplars are removed (deduplicated) before concatenation. No learned distillation, reason-in-documents compression, or distractor-filtering model.
tool_document_engineering: N/A: RaDA does not retrieve tool/skill documents; exemplars are trajectory demonstrations encoded by their task/subtask description (plus state/task metadata) with off-the-shelf embeddings. No synthetic-query augmentation, expanded summaries, weighted-field, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit: the index keys are lightweight task/subtask descriptions and metadata embeddings, while the heavier exemplar trajectory content is loaded into the prompt only for the retrieved top-k. The subtask decomposition further limits how much exemplar content is loaded per call (driving the 4x token efficiency), but the paper does not frame this as a formal progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content mechanism.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A: the retrieval corpus is static (no live-synchronized tool index, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling registry, no CRUD auto-sync). The agent's action space is a fixed programmatic interface (action_type(ID, text) with click/move/type for CompWoB and click/select/type for Mind2Web).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A: RaDA does not model inter-tool dependencies; it retrieves trajectory exemplars, not tools. Subtask ordering/sequencing is handled by the decompositional planner and verifier, not by a tool-dependency graph.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation (in-context demonstrations): retrieved exemplars are injected into the LLM prompt as demonstrations -- for RaD they contextualize the decomposition prompt (P_piD = [instructional prompt, phi(T,E)]); for RaA they implement each subtask function pi_{Q_T} by serving as the demonstrations conditioning grounded action generation (a_1..a_t <- pi_{Q_T}(.|phi(Q_T,E))). The retrieved exemplars replace human-engineered few-shot prompts; no training signal is derived from them.
planning_integration: Hierarchical, retrieve-then-plan-then-(retrieve-then-act): planning is disentangled into two stages -- (1) Retrieval-augmented Task Decomposition (RaD) uses task-level retrieved exemplars to produce a high-level set of subtasks; (2) Retrieval-augmented Action Generation (RaA) iterates over subtasks, at each step reformulating a subtask-compositional query, retrieving subtask-scoped exemplars, generating grounded actions, executing them, and using a subtask-completion verifier to update plan state. Retrieval is interfaced at both the plan (decomposition) level and the per-subtask grounded-action level (subtask-level interleaving), not inside MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-subtask within a rollout: retrieval is woven in at the subtask granularity -- one retrieval for decomposition (per-task) and then one retrieval per subtask iteration during action generation (the subtask-compositional query is reformulated and re-retrieved each loop iteration, after the verifier checks completion). It is not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-individual-tool-call below the subtask level.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar with compositional re-querying: retrieved exemplars are reused as in-context demonstrations (not edited). 'Adaptation' to a new/complex task is achieved structurally -- by decomposing the task into subtasks and dynamically re-composing the retrieval query per subtask (subtask-compositional query) and tracking completion via the verifier -- rather than by an LLM rewriting/repairing a retrieved case. No execution-feedback case-revision, critic-guided rewrite, or RL-reuse finetuning of cases.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw trajectory demonstrations injected as text: retrieved exemplars are surfaced as raw (sub-)trajectory demonstrations of interactions in the web environment (task/subtask description plus action sequences/HTML interactions) placed in the prompt. Not distilled strategies, executable skills, or latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw (sub-)trajectory / single demonstration: the retrieved unit is a concrete demonstration trajectory (task- or subtask-level). The ABSTRACTION in RaDA comes from the planner's high-level subtask decomposition, but the retrieved items themselves are raw demonstrations, not distilled strategies/insights or rules.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Structural / compositional decomposition plus a subtask-completion verifier: by retrieving subtask-scoped exemplars and grounding actions per subtask, RaDA reduces irrelevant whole-trajectory context (vs. Synapse), and the verifier (an instruction-prompted LLM over the last-k steps + remaining subtasks) checks subtask completion before reformulating the next query, mitigating drift. There is no retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator/self-reflection model, or reason-in-documents refinement.
memory_type: episodic (static): a pre-collected episodic store of past task/subtask trajectories used as the retrieval corpus. It is read-only at inference (no skill-library induction, no graph, no latent memory).
write_back: False: RaDA does not store new experiences/cases/skills into memory at inference. The retrieval corpus is fixed (offline-collected successful trajectories); the Limitations section explicitly notes that a framework which also collects new exemplars is future work.
online_growth: No: the retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is frozen after offline construction. The verifier-maintained set of completed subtasks C is transient per-task state, not a persistent growing memory.
write_back_trigger: Never: no write-back event occurs. The corpus is constructed offline from successful trajectories and remains static during inference; no on-success, on-failure, per-step, reflective, or human-validated write is performed at test time.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only: the retrieval corpus is built exclusively from SUCCESSFUL trajectories (48 successful MiniWoB base-task trajectories for CompWoB; Mind2Web training-set trajectories). Failed/negative experiences are not stored or retrieved; there is no failure-contrastive or corrective-rule memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only-offline: stored entries are not mutated after writing (the corpus is fixed offline). No dedup-merge (beyond the RaA-baseline's prompt-time exemplar deduplication), delta-update, refine-overwrite, forget-prune, or link-and-evolve at the memory level.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval/exemplar-selection is a fixed dense-similarity top-k (k=3) over frozen embeddings, not a learned/RL-optimized policy. RaDA's learned/dynamic element is the LLM-driven decomposition and subtask-compositional query reformulation, but the retriever itself is fixed similarity ranking (the paper notes retriever finetuning as future work).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent, single-model private memory; no memory/experience sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: CompWoB (50 compositional web-automation tasks built by combining 2-8 base MiniWoB easy tasks, categorized as two-way (20), three-way (10), n-way (5), transition (5), easy-medium two-way (10); evaluated in Original and Reverse orderings; full-set runs use 912 examples via official Synapse logs) and Mind2Web (crowdsourced human interaction tasks on diverse real websites; cross-domain generalization split and a complex subset selected by task-complexity rank). Retrieval corpora: 48 base MiniWoB-task trajectories (CompWoB) and Mind2Web training-set trajectories (Mind2Web). Backbones: GPT-3.5-turbo-0613, GPT-4-0613 (RaA ablation and Mind2Web use gpt-3.5-turbo-16k-0613).
benchmark_family: web (CompWoB is MiniWoB-derived compositional web automation; Mind2Web is a real-website generalist web-agent benchmark). Both fall under the web-agent / web-navigation family.
baselines: RCI (Recursive Criticism and Improvement; Kim et al., 2023 -- prior SOTA reported in Furuta et al. 2023), AdaPlanner (Sun et al., 2023 -- adaptive post-hoc plan repair), Synapse (Zheng et al., 2024b -- trajectory-as-exemplar prompting with retrieval; closest baseline / pure RaA), and MindAct (Deng et al., 2023 -- the Mind2Web baseline agent, multiple-choice action formulation; used on Mind2Web). Internal ablation baselines: RaA (RaD ablated) and RaD (RaA ablated).
key_metrics: CompWoB: task success rate (%) in Original and Reverse settings, broken down by compositional task type. Mind2Web: element accuracy (Element Acc.), operation F1 (Operation F1), and step success rate (Step SR), macro-averaged across tasks. Statistical significance via paired t-test (P<.001, marked with asterisks). Also context-token efficiency (average/max tokens per LLM call, for exemplars-only and total).
headline_result: On CompWoB, RaDA significantly outperforms all baselines: with GPT-3.5-turbo it reaches 63.6% success (Original) and 49.0% (Reverse) vs. the best baseline RCI at 28.7% / 19.2% (Synapse 25.4% / 16.0%); with GPT-4 RaDA reaches 68.6% (Original) and 57.8% (Reverse) vs. RCI 56.0% / 43.5%. All RaDA improvements are statistically significant (P<.001, paired t-test). On Mind2Web's complex subset (GPT-3.5) RaDA reaches Element Acc. 30.13 / Operation F1 58.18 / Step SR 26.71 vs. Synapse 24.73 / 37.78 / 21.34 and MindAct 9.76 / 55.43 / 8.46.
ablations: Component ablations on CompWoB (GPT-3.5): RaDA (full) = 63.6 (Original) / 49.0 (Reverse); RaA (ablate RaD, subtask-level retrieval but grounds all steps simultaneously) = 38.0 / 23.8; RaD (ablate RaA, decompositional planner with a FIXED set of 5 exemplars: 3 easy + 1 medium + 1 hard) = 50.0 / 37.8 -- showing subtask decomposition and dynamic exemplar retrieval are complementary and both necessary. Per-task-type breakdown (Table 5) shows baselines collapse on n-way/transition/easy-medium and in the Reverse setting (e.g., Synapse Transition 0.0), while RaDA stays robust. Context-token efficiency ablation (Table 6): RaDA uses 1259.8 avg exemplar tokens / 1969.4 avg total tokens per call vs. RaA 3483.5 / 4110.1 (~4x per-call computational efficiency); RaA's long context forces use of the 16k model.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task metrics are reported (success rate; element accuracy / operation F1 / step SR). No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately for the retriever.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome, with some process: primary metrics are outcome-based (task/step success rate, element accuracy, operation F1). Some process-level signal is reported via the CompWoB per-compositional-task-type breakdown (Table 5), the Mind2Web action-step-count complexity analysis (Fig. 2), and qualitative analysis; but there is no formal reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strong efficiency emphasis: an LLM inference call in RaDA uses on average < half the tokens of RaA (1969.4 vs 4110.1 total; 1259.8 vs 3483.5 exemplar tokens), giving ~4x per-call computational efficiency (due to quadratic attention scaling), while RaA's long concatenated exemplars exceed the 4096-token turbo limit and require gpt-3.5-turbo-16k. Per-task total tokens are ~2x higher for RaDA (7285.76 vs 4582.31) because it makes one call per subtask, but RaDA is still more compute-efficient per call and far more accurate. The full-set CompWoB (912 examples) was run on official Synapse logs due to high API costs.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k selection: top-k = 3 exemplars retrieved per query (a fixed hyperparameter, following Synapse). Context budget is managed structurally via subtask decomposition so each call loads only subtask-scoped exemplars (avg ~1260 exemplar tokens per call, fitting within the 4096-token turbo limit), in contrast to whole-trajectory concatenation that exceeds it. The RaD ablation uses a fixed static set of 5 exemplars. No adaptive/precision-driven k or reranked-then-truncated budget.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (RaDA is a method paper, not a benchmark-construction paper; it evaluates on existing benchmarks). For context: CompWoB (Furuta et al., 2023) systematically combines 2-8 MiniWoB easy base tasks into 50 compositional tasks (full set 912 examples) with Original/Reverse orderings; Mind2Web (Deng et al., 2023) is crowdsourced human demonstrations on real websites with a cross-domain split and a complexity-ranked subset.
builds_on: Synapse (Zheng et al., 2024b -- trajectory-as-exemplar retrieval prompting; RaDA reuses its dense retriever setup and corpora and treats it as the pure-RaA baseline); ReAct (Yao et al., 2023 -- interleaved reasoning/acting for agents) and Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); decomposition prompting line: Least-to-Most (Zhou et al., 2023), DecomP (Khot et al., 2023), Plan-and-Solve (Wang et al., 2023), Drozdov et al. (2022); demonstration retrieval / DSP (Khattab et al., 2022), UDR (Li et al., 2023), Dr.ICL (Luo et al., 2023); Dense Passage Retrieval (Karpukhin et al., 2020) for the retriever; in-context learning (Brown et al., 2020). Cognitive inspiration: Lachmy et al. (2022), Zhao et al. (2022), Sumers et al. (2023, cognitive architectures for language agents).
contrasts_with: Synapse (whole-trajectory retrieval that fails on unseen/complex tasks and overflows context); RCI (high human-annotation effort, self-refinement, no compositional generalization -- prior SOTA); AdaPlanner (few-shot post-hoc plan repair, high human effort); DecomP (compositional generalization but requires extensive manual decomposition exemplars and is hard to apply to interactive tasks); MindAct (Mind2Web few-shot multiple-choice baseline). Positioning summarized in Table 1: RaDA targets compositional generalization with NO manual annotation and SHORT input length, unlike DECOMP (high effort), RCI (high effort, no comp. gen.), and Synapse (no effort but long input, no comp. gen.).
lineage: Sits in the retrieval-augmented agent-planning lineage (RAG-for-planning / agentic task-solving, group C_rag_planning): it extends the trajectory-as-exemplar retrieval paradigm of Synapse by introducing retrieval-augmented task DECOMPOSITION plus subtask-level (compositional-query) retrieval-augmented action generation, fusing the decomposition-planning lineage (Least-to-Most / DecomP) with exemplar-retrieval ICL (DSP / UDR / Dr.ICL) to attack compositional generalization in web agents. Precursor/sibling to step-wise / sub-trajectory retrieval agents (e.g., TRAD).
